fields.acceptance: Tests: go test -trimpath -p 2 -count=1 ./internal/model ./internal/check passes. A new TestAsIsSeedWhatIfFrom in internal/model, over a log with a landed base, two in-flight change sets where one depends on the other, one in-flight change set whose ops no longer apply and a duplicate handle, shows that AsIsSeed's Model and problems equal AsIs's and that WhatIfFrom over its seed equals WhatIf (model and problems) for every in-flight change set. A new TestWhatIfOnceMatches in internal/check, over the same shape of log plus an in-flight link whose ends its type does not allow, shows check's in-flight findings listed exactly. Failure case: an in-flight change set whose what-if has problems, and a bad in-flight link, are each reported once, not twice. Profile, before any code change and again after: go build -trimpath -o $TMPDIR/rhiza-x ./cmd/rhiza, then in this repo's main checkout RHIZA_CPUPROFILE=$TMPDIR/check.prof $TMPDIR/rhiza-x check and go tool pprof -top -cum $TMPDIR/rhiza-x $TMPDIR/check.prof. The commit's Checks: block gives /usr/bin/time -f '%e s' for both builds, and the cumulative shares of store.ReadLog, changeset.FoldLog, model.WhatIf/WhatIfFrom, model.asIs and checker.render before and after. After the change, model.WhatIf no longer appears under check.Run. Touches internal/model/seed.go, internal/check/check.go and their tests. Must not change what check reports, its order or its --json shape.
fields.statement: rhiza check builds the as-is view once, with model.AsIsSeed (internal/model/seed.go, new: the as-is Model, its problems and a model.Seed built in memory), and each in-flight change set's what-if once from that seed with model.WhatIfFrom, and the in-flight problems pass (checker.model, internal/check/check.go:384) and the in-flight links pass (checker.inFlightLinks, :456) share those views instead of each calling model.WhatIf

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath -p 2 -count=1 ./internal/store passes. A new TestReadEntriesParallelSame, over a log of a few hundred entries with an unreadable file, an entry that does not decode and an entry whose ID does not match its path, shows the parallel result deep-equals the serial one. go test -race -trimpath -p 2 -count=1 ./internal/store -run ReadEntries is clean. Failure case: with GOMAXPROCS=1 it decodes on one worker and still returns the same Log. Measure, with @{01M7GFXTMA9VHC2FAQB33P1KA1} already in: build $TMPDIR/rhiza-x as in @{01M7GFXTMA9VHC2FAQB33P1KA1} and record in the commit's Checks: block /usr/bin/time -f '%e s' $TMPDIR/rhiza-x check in this repo's main checkout, before and after this leaf, and store.ReadLog's cumulative pprof share. After this leaf, check takes at most half of the 13.8 s measured on 2026-11-15 on the 4-core VM. Touches internal/store/read.go and its tests. Must not add a dependency or change the order or content of Entries or Problems.
fields.statement: store.ReadEntries (internal/store/read.go:97) decodes entry files on up to four workers (bounded by GOMAXPROCS), the way the index's listing already stats folders in parallel, and returns the same Log as the serial decode: the same entries and problems in the same order

fields.reasoning: Only internal/index builds a model.Seed today (loadSeed, from its stored rows), and check reads the log files through store.ReadLog, runs on a fresh clone in CI and needs no daemon or index, so it cannot borrow the index's seed. AsIsState already returns the State half of a Seed, so an AsIsSeed beside it in seed.go is the small step. The strict engine (internal/model) is the spec, so WhatIfFrom over this seed must give exactly WhatIf's model and problems; a model test holds that.
fields.statement: rhiza check gets its as-is seed from a new model.AsIsSeed(sets) in internal/model/seed.go, returning the as-is Model, its problems and a model.Seed built in memory from the folded change sets, and never from internal/index

fields.reasoning: The 2026-11-15 profile (13.8 s wall) puts model.WhatIf at 46% of samples and model.asIs at 26%, while the decode (store.ReadLog) is 7%. So the what-if change carries the gain and the parallel decode adds about a second at most. A fixed '5 s' guess made before profiling could be missed for reasons outside this change set (textRefs, FoldLog, GC). Half the measured time is a target that the profile supports. Ordering the decode leaf second lets one measurement show the combined result.
fields.statement: The time target for this change set is measured after both leaves: rhiza check on this repo's main checkout takes at most half the 13.8 s measured on 2026-11-15, on the 4-core VM. read-entries-parallel is built after check-whatif-once so its measurement covers both
